questions.q: What is the real point of "defense in depth" as a security principle?
options: It means ACLs are no longer necessary once other layers exist
It only applies to physical security, not software platforms
Multiple independent layers each catch different failure modes, so one layer breaking doesn't mean total compromise
It means every layer must use exactly the same enforcement mechanism
questions.explain: Defense in depth relies on independent layers catching different risks — a gap in one layer doesn't automatically compromise the whole system if another layer contains it.

questions.q: Why is a UI Policy alone not sufficient to enforce a field requirement, per this lesson?
options: A UI Policy runs client-side in the browser and can be bypassed by a direct API call, unlike a server-side Data Policy or Business Rule
UI Policies don't exist on the Now Platform
UI Policies only work on the Service Catalog, never on forms
UI Policies are slower than Data Policies and should never be used
questions.explain: Client-side enforcement (UI Policy, Client Script) can be skipped by anyone calling the API directly; server-side enforcement (Data Policy, Business Rule) cannot.

questions.q: What does Application Scope isolation actually protect against, as a distinct layer from ACLs?
options: It protects against weak passwords
It replaces the need for any ACLs within the scoped application
It only matters for MID Server connections, not custom applications
It protects against a scoped application's tables and APIs being reached by other applications, unless cross-scope access is explicitly granted
questions.explain: Scope isolation is a separate layer from ACLs: by default, one scoped app's tables and APIs are invisible to other apps unless cross-scope access explicitly allows it.

questions.q: Why does the MID Server count as a security layer in this lesson's five-layer model?
options: It encrypts all data stored in ServiceNow tables
It lets the instance reach on-premises systems through an outbound-only connection, so no inbound firewall port into the ServiceNow cloud is ever needed
It replaces the need for authentication on integrated systems
It is only relevant to Application Scope isolation, not network security
questions.explain: The MID Server is a network-security layer: its outbound-only design means your firewall never needs an inbound port open to the ServiceNow cloud.

questions.q: What distinguishes a security architect's question from an administrator's question, per this lesson's closing point?
options: An administrator asks whether one ACL is configured correctly; an architect asks which other layers would still contain the damage if that ACL were slightly wrong
An architect never configures ACLs directly
There is no real difference between the two roles
An architect only cares about authentication, not ACLs
questions.explain: Seeing the whole layered model — and knowing which layers back up which others — is the distinction this lesson draws between administering and architecting security.
